subject: Re: FinPay - Follow-up: competitive TCO and next tests
messages:
From: Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.ai>
To: Emma Tan <emma.tan@finpay.com>
Cc: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.ai>, Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 30 Jun 2026 15:12:00 -0700
Subject: FinPay discovery recap + next steps (competitive TCO focus)

Emma — thanks again for the call today. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we keep momentum: 

Summary of FinPay priorities from the call:
- High-throughput inference for real-time transaction enrichment (median payload ~150 tokens).
- Hard latency requirement: p95 < 180ms on production traffic.
- Cost sensitivity for mid-term: target <$6 per 1M tokens processed on average, with variability depending on batching and cache hit rate.
- Security & compliance: SOC2 + data residency in us-east required.

Competitive context you raised:
- You are evaluating hyperscaler managed endpoints (HS-API) and InferenceCo’s hosted offering. Key asks are: 1) clear per-1M token unit economics, 2) how batching/caching affects unit cost and latency, 3) recommended next tests.

Proposed next steps:
1) We’ll share a TCO workbook with modeled per-1M token costs under three scenarios (baseline, aggressive batching, high cache hit). Marcus will attach the spreadsheet.
2) Short POE (proof of economics) run: 100k–500k tokens of representative traffic to validate real-world batching/caching behavior and p95 latency.
3) Security checklist: we’ll provide SOC2 attestation and a quick plan for VPC/private deployment if required.

Would you like us to schedule the POE kickoff next week? We can prep the test harness and a short set of prompts.

Thanks,
Aditya Rao
Senior Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
redwood.ai

Attachments: redwood_tco_calc.xlsx (spreadsheet)

From: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.ai>

Subject: RE: FinPay discovery recap + next steps

Adding the initial TCO model and a one-pager on hyperscaler comparison. High-level notes from the modeling (spreadsheet attached):

Model assumptions (baseline):
- Model: open-220B quantized variant we discussed (compatible with Redwood runtime).
- Throughput profile: avg 4 requests/sec during burst windows, median payload 150 tokens, average output 60 tokens.
- Compute pricing: internal GPU amortized + infra (we modeled Dedicated and Hosted modes for apples-to-apples vs hyperscaler).

Preliminary numbers (per-1M tokens generated, include both prompt + completion):
- Redwood hosted (no batching, conservative): $8.40 / 1M tokens
- Redwood hosted (with batching @ 2.5 avg requests/batch, cache hit 10%): $5.10 / 1M tokens
- Redwood hosted (optimized batching + KV prefix caching 30% hit): $3.60 / 1M tokens
- Hyperscaler managed (HS-API) estimate: $10–$14 / 1M tokens (depends on their price sheet and less efficient batching for small payloads)

Latency impact notes:
- Baseline (no batching): p95 ~ 140–170ms (on our selected region with warm caches).
- With batching: p95 can increase ~30–80ms depending on queueing/time-window settings; we have strategies to keep p95 under 180ms while preserving cost benefits (adaptive batching + priority lanes).

See attached 'redwood_tco_calc.xlsx' and 'redwood_vs_hyperscaler.pdf' for the scenario breakdown.

— Marcus
Principal Product Manager, Pricing | Redwood Inference

Attachments: redwood_tco_calc.xlsx, redwood_vs_hyperscaler.pdf

Thanks Aditya and Marcus — useful start. A few clarifying questions before we lock in the POE: 

1) Your per-1M numbers — do they include all infra overhead (eg network egress, storage for KV cache, control plane costs)? Would be great to see line items.
2) Our workload mixes many short prompts; how sensitive are those numbers to queueing delays from batching? We can tolerate some additional latency but p95 must stay <180ms.
3) Can you propose the exact test harness (sample traffic shape, duration, and acceptance criteria) so we can align with our SREs?

Also copying Liam (Eng) and procurement. If you can get the POE plan and line-item TCO today, we can decide about kickoff next week.

Thanks Emma — answers inline and attached a slightly more granular workbook (see redwood_tco_calc.xlsx tabbed by line item). High-level line-item callouts: 

- Included line items: GPU cycles (amortized), memory/kv storage, network egress (estimated 2.5% of costs for typical traffic), control plane ops (small constant overhead in hosted), and licensing/ops for Dedicated when selected. The attached workbook has a toggle for Hosted vs Dedicated.

- Sensitivity to short prompts / batching: short prompts reduce batching efficiency. In our model: baseline (no batching) represents worst-case small prompts -> $8.40 / 1M. With realistic batching (2.0–2.5 avg requests per batch) you see ~$5.10 / 1M. If you can enable prefix KV caching that hits ~25–35% on repeated transaction templates, we get down to ~$3.6 / 1M.

- Latency management: Our runtime supports adaptive batching that prioritizes latency-sensitive requests and opportunistically batches background requests. For your p95 < 180ms requirement, recommended config: max batching window 20ms, priority lane for interactive flows. That preserves ~70–80% of batching benefits while keeping p95 in your SLA. We also recommend a small warm-up run to pre-populate KV cache for top templates.

Proposed POE harness (we've used this with similar fintech customers):
- Traffic shape: 100k tokens in 2–3 hour run with bursts up to 6 RPS; mix 70% short prompts (50–100 tokens), 30% longer (200–400 tokens).
- Acceptance criteria: p95 latency < 180ms; observed per-1M tokens cost within 15% of modeled scenario (we'll run the spreadsheet live).
- Deliverables: raw logs (token counts, batch sizes, cache hits), cost calc export, recommended config for production.

Next steps: If that looks good, propose POE kickoff Tue 2026-07-06 (30–45 minute kickoff w/ SRE). I'll invite a brief walkthrough to align metrics and test harness.
